approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm over molecular graphs whose evaluations are allocated by a fingerprint Gaussian process, both fitted only to this session's own accepted molecules. It keeps the sixty-four best scored molecules, draws breeding parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and for each announced batch of ten it breeds a surplus pool of candidates: with probability 0.45 by recombining connected fragments of two scored parents, with an optional single finishing edit, and otherwise by a random walk of one, two or three successive local graph edits on one scored parent, sampled 0.82/0.15/0.03, where a saturation floor lengthens the walk only after very many consecutive failed attempts for the same pool slot. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is switched off, products are admitted under stable canonical identities with duplicate rejection, and a narrow sulfur rule rejects any product that introduces an outside-envelope sulfur environment its scored generating parents did not already have. A Gaussian process on radius-two integer Morgan counts with a generalized Tanimoto kernel, adaptive score normalization and correlated Thompson sampling then picks the ten pool members to evaluate, and accepted feedback updates the archive and the survivor population. Nothing in it reads the task identity, and nothing reads how well the search is currently going: the walk-length law is the same in a run that is improving and in a run that has stalled.
approach.novelty: One mechanism: make the ordinary single-parent step length conditional on measured stagnation by removal. While the session's own count of consecutive announced batches that failed to raise its best-so-far stands at three or more, every ordinary single-parent proposal of that batch makes exactly one graph edit; the optional second and third edits come back unchanged the moment an announced batch improves again, and the search is bit-for-bit the Parent before the first stall. Siblings that share this trigger changed what the stalled phase selects from or how it scores candidates - a wider candidate pool, eligibility restricted to the best-predicted candidates, contracted or widened posterior residuals, a discarded allocator draw as a path reference - or changed the generator the other way, by lengthening stalled walks or by switching recombination off during stalls. Continuation itself has so far only been removed for an entire run, where it cost a third of a point of panel mean while lifting the campaign's hardest, most score-compressed task. This node is the first to search the stalled phase with a strictly shorter step than the improving phase, which isolates the one dose of that direction the evidence actually points at and leaves the improving phase untouched.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent chooses the length of its ordinary single-parent graph walk from a fixed law that never reads the state of the search, so it spends exactly the same share of its proposals on two- and three-edit walks while the session is improving and while it has measurably stopped improving. Recomputed here from the Parent's own published receipts (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0|1|2/trajectories/*.jsonl and seed-*/logs/*.log) under the unchanged K=3 rule, the Parent announces 91 of its 435 batches with the counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches at or above three, in 29 episodes across 13 of 15 sessions (median_2 5/4/3, deco_hop 0/7/0, drd2_docking 1/9/8, sitagliptin_mpo 4/11/6, zaleplon_mpo 8/13/12; the two deco_hop sessions of seeds 0 and 2 never trigger). Inside those stalled batches it makes 9,463 ordinary single-parent attempts, of which 1,672 execute an optional second or third edit (1,972 continuation calls, 17.7% of in-regime attempts, matching its state-blind 0.82/0.15/0.03 law) and 1,649 of those multi-edit products are admitted to an offspring pool. What that continuation channel is worth during stagnation is unmeasured on this Parent: the only same-Parent measurement with a median_2 direction shortens every walk of the run (n-c070e95b09ef: median_2 0.234662, +0.011975, the largest same-Parent median_2 signal in the lineage, while the panel loses 0.030700 and deco_hop loses 0.0905), the same whole-run shortening on the previous Parent raised median_2 by +0.010627 (n-dbee08307e86), and the opposite stall-gated dose that lengthened stalled walks gained only through one task, with its lengthened products delivering 0.052353 of the 0.599867 in-regime increment (n-e5dba2059cfe, +0.007648). The limiting behaviour this node responds to is therefore a state-blind continuation channel that keeps running precisely in the phase where the Parent's own best-so-far has stopped moving, with no measurement of whether it helps there.

literature_review.conclusion: No literature adoption enters this Candidate. The frozen round-40 review supplies the campaign's stall context but assigns no candidate method to this ablation, and the removal of an inherited optional mutation call needs no external source; the design is justified by the lineage's own measured continuation and stall-gated results and by exposure recomputed from the Parent's receipts.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: This position removes an existing inherited behaviour inside an already published, unchanged trigger; it introduces no model, package, asset or borrowed method, so no search is required and none is claimed. The frozen round-40 review that the ticket carries records the only literature levers it considered for this window - trust-region success/failure hysteresis, fixed-budget variance control, a quantile output transform, scaffold-bucket memory and twin explore/exploit populations - and assigns none of them to this position; its exit-rule adoption is deliberately excluded here so this arm stays comparable with the eight existing same-trigger siblings. The intervention rests entirely on internal evidence: the two completed whole-run continuation removals on this Parent and its predecessor, the stall-gated heavier-walk arm, the stall-gated crossover removal at the same dose, the law-free path reference, and exposure recomputed from the Parent's own published trajectories and diagnostics.

hypothesis: Suppress optional ordinary single-parent mutation continuation during measured stagnation only. In every breeding attempt of a batch announced while the session's own counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches stands at or above K=3, an ordinary single-parent proposal at the inherited saturation floor of one makes exactly one mutate call instead of the sampled one, two or three; the original base-length draw is still made at its original stream position, the escalation schedule above floor one is untouched, and the inherited optional second and third calls are restored exactly in every batch announced outside the regime and before the first activation. The unchanged round-38/39 entry rule and its original exit on the first improving announced batch are reused, so stalled search takes strictly shorter graph walks while improving search is unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Cutting multi-edit walks only during stalls ran exactly; panel +0.0039 rests on zaleplon, median_2 flat, sitagliptin breaches margin
finding_summary.insights:
Where continuation earns its keep. On this Anchor, removing optional multi-edit walks for the whole run cost 0.031 of panel mean. Removing them only while the search is stalled cost nothing (+0.0039). These are dependent single realizations and cannot be added together. Side by side, though, they suggest the channel's value sits in the improving phase, not in stalls. By the registered rule this node classifies stall-phase continuation as harmful presence. Because one cell carries that classification, it is a weak negative and not a case for removing continuation anywhere.

The median_2 lead does not run through stalls. The whole-run removal's +0.012 on median_2 did not reappear. median_2 rarely stalls at K=3 (8 stalled batches over three seeds here, 12 on the Anchor) because it keeps creeping upward in steps of about 0.003. The switch therefore cut only 16 to 73 walks per median_2 session (19 to 88 suppressed edits), and median_2 cell swings of about 0.02 are the size of path noise. A stall-gated change is structurally weak on median_2. If shorter walks really help median_2, they would have to act in the improving phase, where the whole-run removal showed that shortening costs deco_hop and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment explains why walk length is the wrong lever there. The median_2 sessions stay on inherited quinoline-plus-cyclic-imide cores whose leading decorations all score within 0.007 of each other, and the leader moved only from 0.222 to 0.229 over the whole run. Crossing that plateau needs a scaffold-changing move such as building a new ring, not a shorter or longer walk. Two things remain worth testing: a trigger that counts tiny gains as stagnation, computed only from the session's own score scale, and the molecular role's ring-construction gap.

A task-dependent sign. On this Anchor, sitagliptin_mpo and zaleplon_mpo respond in opposite directions to stall-time walk length, and they do so consistently across the two opposite doses. The stall-gated longer-walk sibling gained +0.053 on sitagliptin (all three seeds) and lost 0.010 on zaleplon. This shorter-walk node lost 0.021 on sitagliptin and gained 0.037 on zaleplon. Each is one dependent realization, and single cells can move by about 0.04 from path noise alone. Still, the mirror pattern suggests that no fixed stall-time walk length suits every task. The candidate never knows its task, so the next useful experiment is not another fixed dose. It is a rule that reads this session's own evidence on whether multi-edit products are paying off.

Still open: zaleplon seed 0, the cell that all eight earlier same-trigger siblings lost, rose here from 0.459 to 0.513, and one realization cannot say whether that was the shorter walks or luck. Path noise remains the binding uncertainty. This node's cell spread (standard deviation 0.033) is more than twice that of the single law-free reference (0.015), so a second realization would be needed before the harmful-presence reading is trusted. As a median_2 route, stall-gated continuation removal should stop.
finding_summary.results:
The switch behaved exactly as registered. Thirteen of the fifteen task sessions stalled long enough to trigger it: 84 of 435 announced batches in 29 stall episodes, against 91 batches in 29 episodes on the Anchor's own path. The two decoration-hopping sessions that never stall (seeds 0 and 2) reproduced the Anchor molecule for molecule, including its 0.856 seed-0 endpoint. Every other session matched the Anchor exactly until its first stalled batch. The logged stall state matched an independent recount from the run's own scores in all 435 batches.

Inside stalled batches, all 8,036 single-parent mutation attempts made exactly one edit. 1,461 of them (18%) had drawn a two- or three-edit walk and were cut short, suppressing 1,686 edits. No multi-edit product entered a pool, where the Anchor had pooled 1,593 in its stalled batches. Outside stalls the walk-length mix stayed at the inherited 82/15/3 percent. The shortened walks did reach the oracle. Their first products filled 1,365 pool slots and the allocator picked 96 of them, about twice the rate at which it picked the Anchor's multi-edit products (7.0% versus 3.5%). Of those 96, 9 beat their parent and 5 briefly raised the session best, but none became a final endpoint. Inside stalls, the overall parent-beating rate (8.8% versus 8.6%) and the number of new bests (25 versus 28) were essentially the Anchor's.

On scores, the fifteen-cell mean rose by 0.0039 (0.6003 versus 0.5965). That lands in the pre-registered 'harmful presence' band (at least +0.002), the opposite of the decrease the plan expected, but it is fragile. The seed macros moved +0.0002, -0.0060 and +0.0174. Six cells rose, six fell and three were unchanged. The gain comes from zaleplon_mpo (+0.037 mean; cells +0.054, -0.035 and +0.094). Dropping the single zaleplon seed-2 cell turns the panel to -0.0025, and the other twelve cells average -0.0045.

median_2, the brief's target, did not move: 0.2221 versus the Anchor's 0.2227 (-0.0006; cells +0.014, +0.003 and -0.019). That is far short of the +0.010 goal, and the seed-2 cell is below the Anchor. Three of the four protected tasks held their margins: deco_hop (+0.0038), drd2_docking (+0.0001) and zaleplon_mpo (+0.0373). sitagliptin_mpo fell 0.0211 (0.5837 versus 0.6048), just past its 0.02 margin, almost entirely from seed 0 (-0.054).

molecular.headline: Inherited cores decorated with heteroatom-bound halogens, hydrazides, nitroso and strained fused rings; only one objective reaches real drug chemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Read the digest and then all fifteen supplied child trajectories (three seeds x five objectives, 300 records each, ten initial and 290 optimizer proposals per session) plus all fifteen published Parent trajectories for n-1744a1494180; the digest lists no tasks without trajectories, and every path in focus.artifacts.this_node_trajectories and focus.artifacts.parent_trajectories exists and was read. context.comparison reports the Child complete on seeds 0/1/2 and paired complete against the code Parent on the same three seeds, so every comparison below is a complete-pairing chemical observation and never a causal or activation claim. Across 4350 optimizer proposals the output is uniformly ring-rich and aromatic: the per-task molecule-level incidences in the digest are 0.96-0.98 for ring closure and 0.95-0.97 for aromatic atoms, mean SMILES length 41.7-58.4, and my own RDKit reading of the same files gives a median of 3-6 rings and 2-4 aromatic rings per molecule at 24-34 heavy atoms and 340-470 Da. Size, ring count and mass therefore sit inside ordinary medicinal-chemistry range, and the molecules fail elsewhere: the generator reaches heteroatom and halogen content through bonds a chemist would not draw. Not one of the 4350 proposals contains a trifluoromethyl group, while two sessions put a halogen directly on nitrogen in 447 and 379 of their 870 molecules (20-38 in the other three); nitroso appears 240 times on one objective where nitro appears zero times; halogen-oxygen, peroxide, N-N and N-O single bonds recur in 7-78 molecules a session; and ring-forming edits produce three- and four-membered rings fused onto aromatics (201-433 per session) and eight- to twelve-membered rings (up to 222) rather than new five- and six-membered heteroaromatics. Diversity is moderate over the whole set (221-585 distinct Bemis-Murcko scaffolds per session) but narrow at the top: the thirty best-scoring molecules of a session share only 6-12 scaffolds on four objectives, and the leaders are often halogen-permutation siblings whose scores are identical to four decimal places. Every session also spends 4-32 evaluations on one- to five-heavy-atom fragments. The digest's stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0-0.0011 are text readings: no proposal annotates configuration or formal charge, although RDKit perceives unassigned stereocentres in 36-96 percent of the molecules on four objectives. Chemistry-quality chips below are my structural reading, not a computed synthesis or property calculation.

per_task.generated_character: 870 optimizer proposals, median 25 heavy atoms and about 376 Da, molecule-level incidences 0.963 ring closure, 0.960 aromatic atoms and 0.902 halogen. One family dominates the top: a 2-cyano-4-alkoxy-3-methylbenzene ring joined by a two- or three-atom linker (CH2CH2, CH=CH, CH=C(F/Br) or N=CH) to an N-aryl amide whose amide nitrogen carries NH2, NHOH, Cl or a cyanamide. 704 of 870 carry an aryl methyl or ethyl ether, 204 a nitrile (the Parent set has 1), 444 a secondary amide NH, and 447 a nitrogen-halogen bond; 112 retain the indole-2-carboxamide the initial pool supplied. The single best molecule, COc1ccc(CCC(=O)N(C#N)c2ccccc2)c(C)c1C#N at 0.531, is halogen-free with formula C19H17N3O2, two isolated benzene rings, two nitriles and an N-cyanoanilide. Final-batch members stay in the same family at 0.39-0.47, one of them, COC1C=C(CCC(=O)N(C#N)c2ccccc2)C(C)=C1C#N at 0.472, with the aromatic ring opened to a methoxycyclopentadiene.
liabilities: N-amino amide (hydrazide) in 133 of 870 and in nine of the twelve digest leaders, for example CCOc1ccc(CC(=O)N(N)c2cccc(F)c2)c(C)c1C#N at 0.498
halogen on nitrogen, including an N-bromo indole plus an N-chloro anilide in CCc1ccc2c(cc(C(=O)CN(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2Br)c1OC at 0.513
an N-amino-N-hydroxy amide in CCOc1ccc(C(F)=CC(=O)N(NO)c2cccc(Br)c2)c(C)c1C#N at 0.455
vinyl and benzylic halides, for example the CH2Br of COc1cc(N)c(C=CC(=O)N(N)c2cccc(F)c2)c(CBr)c1C#N at 0.423
a dearomatized cyclopentadiene core in the last proposal, COC1C=C(CCC(=O)N(C#N)c2ccccc2)C(C)=C1C#N
missing_features: no fused nitrogen-bridged bicyclic heteroaromatic: only 5 of 870 proposals contain any five-membered aromatic azole and 7 of 870 a pyrimidine ring, so the bicycle is never assembled
no N-alkyl acetamide on an aniline nitrogen; the amide nitrogen instead carries NH2, NHOH, Cl or a cyanamide
no halogen-free composition on all but a handful of members: 758 of the 827 molecules above 15 heavy atoms carry a halogen
no ring fused to the nitrile-bearing ring; the leaders keep two separate benzene rings joined by a flexible chain
no basic or acidic centre at all: only 53 of 870 carry a basic amine and 0 a carboxylic acid
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 0.0 to 0.531 with median 0.319. The gradient rewards a compact 24-26 heavy-atom two-ring molecule carrying an aryl alkyl ether, an aromatic nitrile and one amide, and it is blind to halogen identity: CCOc1ccc(C(Br)=CC(=O)N(N)c2cccc(F)c2)c(C)c1C#N and CCOc1ccc(C(F)=CC(=O)N(N)c2cccc(Br)c2)c(C)c1C#N both score 0.5169, and two further F/Br pairs tie at 0.4975 and 0.4964. The one member that drops every halogen is also the only one above 0.52, so the halogen decoration the whole set carries is at best neutral. The floor is pure fragments: Br, ClCl, FBr, S and C#C all return 0.0, and ten to eleven such proposals per seed consume evaluations that teach nothing.

per_task.generated_character: The largest aromatic set: 870 proposals, median 32 heavy atoms and 448 Da, 0.974 ring-closure and 0.974 aromatic-atom incidence, 608 of 870 containing a direct aryl-aryl bond and 286 a pyrimidine ring. Two separate basins. The seed-0 leaders are a pentacyclic pyrazolo-fused thioxo-pyrimidinone linked to a chloroquinazoline that carries an aryl O-F bond and an N-CH(F)-O-CH2Cl arm, as in O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 at 0.856. The seed-2 leaders are a different object: a cyclopropa-fused benzene bearing two nitroso groups, attached through a CH(N=O) aminal to an acetyl- and formyl-substituted azacyclobutene-fused ring with a methoxyethyl or propargyloxyethyl tail, as in COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2 at 0.644. Across the set nitroso occurs 240 times, thiocarbonyl 206, three- or four-membered rings 201, chloromethyl 75, peroxide 78 and O-F 20, while nitro, sulfonamide and sulfone occur zero times. The same three 0.856 molecules are the leaders of the paired Parent session on seed 0, so on this objective the two sets end on identical chemistry.
liabilities: aryl hypofluorite O-F bonds in every seed-0 leader, for example O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)F)C3 at 0.856
C-nitroso groups on an arene and on an aminal carbon, three per molecule in the seed-2 leaders such as CC(=O)c1c(C)c(C(N=O)Nc2cc3c(N=O)cc2-3)c2c(c1CCOC=O)C=N2 at 0.6416
cyclopropa-fused arene strain, the cc3c(...)cc2-3 motif carried by all six final molecules
thiocarbonyl plus chloromethyl ether in the same molecule, O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(CCl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3 at 0.856
an exposed thiol tautomer in CC1c2c3c(nn2-c2ncnc4cc(OF)c(Cl)cc24)N1C(=CS)N(C(F)OCCl)C3=O at 0.800
aldehydes on crowded aromatics in 109 of 870, for example CC(=O)c1c(C=O)c(C(N=O)Nc2cc3c(N=O)cc2-3)c2c(c1CCOCCF)C=N2 at 0.633
missing_features: no sulfonyl or sulfonamide linker anywhere in the 870 proposals, and no carboxylic acid
no unstrained ring fusion in the top band: 18 of the 30 best molecules contain a three- or four-membered ring
no conventional five-membered aromatic heterocycle replacement: thiophene 0 and furan 4 of 870
no basic amine centre: 39 of 870 carry one and only one of the thirty best
no halogen placed as a makeable group; the leaders carry O-F and CH(F)-O-CH2Cl instead of aryl-F or CF3
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 0.5 to 0.856, median 0.597, and the 0.5 end is a floor that any fragment reaches: C, Cl, C=C, N=O, C#CCO and N#CCl all score exactly 0.5, so half the scale carries no structural information. What separates the basins is the whole scaffold, not the decoration: the fused tricyclic-plus-chloroazaquinazoline family sits at 0.799-0.856 and the nitroso family at 0.607-0.644, while inside a basin large substituent swaps barely move the score (C(F)OCCl replaced by C(F)F stays at 0.856; CCOC=O replaced by CCOC=S stays at 0.6416). The gradient therefore rewards one specific fused polycyclic topology bearing a chlorinated azaquinazoline, and the search has no remaining handle once it is in a basin.

per_task.generated_character: The only session that ends on recognisable medicinal chemistry. 870 proposals, median 29 heavy atoms and 441 Da, 0.974 ring-closure and 0.967 aromatic-atom incidence, 0.983 halogen incidence, and a saturated nitrogen ring in 471 of 870. The leaders are 1,4-diazepane or 1,5-diazocane rings carrying a 3-chlorophenyl group on a quaternary benzylic carbon and an N-phenethyl arm bearing 3-bromo-5-methylthio or 3-bromo-2-hydroxy-5-alkyl substitution, for example CCC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)CN(CCc2cc(Br)cc(SC)c2)CCCCN1 and CSc1cc(Br)cc(CCN2CCCCNC(C)(c3cccc(Cl)c3)C2)c1 at 0.999996 and 0.999994. All thirty of the best-scoring molecules carry a basic amine and only two carry any flagged group; median QED of that top band is 0.48. The low end is the initial pool's 3,5-dichlorobenzenesulfonyl prolinamide chemistry, for example CC(=O)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.0002. The final batch has drifted into a second chromane/benzofuran-amine family, CCCc1cc(Br)cc(-c2ccc3c(c2)OC(CO)CC3N(C)CCC)c1Cl at 0.988.
liabilities: aryl bromide plus thioanisole in the top molecules, CSc1cc(Br)cc(CCN2CCCCNC(c3cccc(Cl)c3)C2)c1 at 0.999986, both metabolically and promiscuity liable
a 1,5-diazocane eight-membered diamine ring in the best molecule CCC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)CN(CCc2cc(Br)cc(SC)c2)CCCCN1
benzylic chlorides in four of the six final proposals, for example CCCN(C)C1CC(C)(CO)Oc2cc(-c3cc(F)cc(CCl)c3)ccc21 at 0.9218
an exocyclic enamine on a 2,3-dihydropyrrole in C=C(C1=CCN1CCC)N(C)C1CCOc2cc(-c3cc(Cl)cc(CF)c3)c(Cl)cc21 at 0.9788
an aminomethyl plus dearomatized ring in CCCN(C)C1CC(CN)Oc2cc(C3=CC(CCl)=CC(F)=C(N)C3)ccc21 at 0.450
missing_features: no configuration at the quaternary benzylic carbon of any leader, although that centre is stereogenic in all of them
no trifluoromethyl or trifluoromethoxy group in the 870 proposals; aryl lipophilicity is carried by Br, Cl and SMe only
no piperazine and no piperidine ring in the whole child session (the paired Parent session has 3 and 23)
no heteroaryl replacement for the pendant phenyl rings: 49 of 870 contain a pyridine and 1 an azole
no amide, sulfonamide or acid in the leaders, so the whole high-scoring band is a flat lipophilic diamine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 0.0002 to 0.99999, median 0.689, and the whole range is covered by one transition: from an aryl sulfonyl pyrrolidine amide with no basic nitrogen to a protonatable secondary or tertiary amine in a six- to eight-membered ring flanked by two lipophilic halogenated aryl groups. Among molecules above 15 heavy atoms the 836 halogenated ones have median 0.739 against 0.017 for the 5 halogen-free ones. The objective is saturated, so the only information left in the trajectory is the cost of breaking the motif: the final-batch pair CCCN(C)C1CC(CN)Oc2cc(-c3cc(F)cc(CCl)c3)ncc21 at 0.898 and CCCN(C)C1CC(CN)Oc2cc(C3=CC(CCl)=CC(F)=C(N)C3)ccc21 at 0.450 differ only in that the second has its pendant aryl ring opened to an aminocyclohexadiene, and that single dearomatization costs half the score.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The most compressed set: span 0.0 to 0.2287 with median 0.188, and the entire optimizer run moves the leader from 0.222 to 0.229. Everything built on the inherited quinoline-plus-cyclic-imide core sits in a 0.19-0.23 band, and the digest's twelve leaders differ only in alkyl and alkoxy decoration of the saturated imide ring (C43CC, C43C, C43OCC and an N-F variant all within 0.007 of each other). Halogenation is irrelevant here: among molecules above 15 heavy atoms the 120 halogenated ones have median 0.193 and the 727 halogen-free ones 0.190. The only large drop is to the fragments, C, N, OO and C#C at 0.0, so the trajectory offers almost no usable gradient and the search spends it on ring inflation.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 7.7e-27 to 0.640 with median 0.166, and fluorine count drives it. Among molecules above 15 heavy atoms the 742 halogenated ones have median 0.229 against 0.003 for the 83 halogen-free ones, and the 379 that carry a nitrogen-halogen bond have the highest median of all at 0.253 and hold the top score, so the gradient as the optimizer sees it actively pays for fluorine on nitrogen. Within the leading family the moves are small and reversible: COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1C=C(F)CN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F at 0.638 against COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=C(F)CN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F at 0.630 is one extra fluorine on a ring carbon, and swapping an N-F for an N-CH3 in COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=C(F)CN1)c(=O)n(C)c(=N)n2F costs 0.03. The final batch shows how brittle the family is, falling to 0.037 for Cc1c2c(=N)n(CCF)c(=O)n3c2c-3n1C1(F)C(F)=CC=C1CCF and to 0.0 for the fragment CC(F)Cl.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 optimizer proposals of this node, and all 4350 of the paired code Parent, not one molecule contains a trifluoromethyl group and only 47 contain any CF2 or CHF2 carbon. Halogen instead goes onto heteroatoms: two sessions place a halogen directly on nitrogen in 447 and 379 of their 870 molecules (352 of the latter are N-F), the other three in 20-38, and 0-57 per session carry a halogen bonded to oxygen. Where halogen content tracks reward, the N-halogenated molecules above 15 heavy atoms hold the highest median score of any subset (0.253 against 0.229 for halogenated molecules generally) and hold the session best, so the generator is being paid for a bond no chemist would draw.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never builds a polyhalogenated carbon; it reaches halogen content by bonding halogen to nitrogen or oxygen.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen-adding edits should place halogens on carbon and should be able to install them as a complete group (CF3, CHF2, OCF3, polyfluorinated ring) in one step, while heteroatom-halogen products are refused at admission unless an accepted scored parent already carried that environment. That changes what fraction of a halogen-rewarding gradient is reachable through makeable chemistry rather than through N-X and O-X artifacts.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one session the digest leaders contain three F/Br pairs that differ in nothing else and tie to ten decimal places: 0.5168582743858251 twice, 0.49753394639502424 twice, 0.4964011584894659 twice. In another, replacing C(F)OCCl with C(F)F leaves 0.8561477222467935 unchanged, and replacing an ester CCOC=O with a thioester CCOC=S leaves 0.6415763673890609 unchanged. Each pair consumed two evaluations from a 290-proposal budget.
transferable_gaps.gap: Single-halogen identity swaps are generated as if they were distinct candidates, and they return score-identical siblings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the proposal pool an identity notion coarser than canonical SMILES for interchangeable terminal decorations, so that a halogen-for-halogen or chalcogen-for-chalcogen substitution on the same skeleton is treated as the already-evaluated molecule unless something else changed. Evaluations then buy new skeletons instead of re-pricing the same one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the session whose reward most clearly tracks a fused bicyclic, only 5 of 870 proposals contain any five-membered aromatic azole and 7 of 870 a pyrimidine ring, while 112 keep the indole-2-carboxamide the initial molecules supplied and the top band never leaves two separate benzene rings joined by a chain. Where fused heteroaromatics do appear in quantity (799 of 870 pyrimidine-containing molecules in another session) they are inherited, not constructed. Thiophene appears 3 times and furan 9 times in 4350 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot close a new five- or six-membered aromatic heterocycle, so it only decorates the fused cores the initial pool gave it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add a ring-construction operator that closes and fuses conventional five- and six-membered aromatic heterocycles, drawing the closure from a library of real ring systems rather than from arbitrary bond addition between two atoms. Without it the reachable set is the initial population's scaffolds plus acyclic decoration, whatever the gradient asks for.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per session 21-433 molecules contain a three- or four-membered ring and up to 222 contain a ring of eight atoms or more. This is not confined to the discarded tail: 18 of the 30 best molecules in one session and 23 of 30 in another contain a three- or four-membered ring, including cyclopropa-fused arenes (the cc3c(...)cc2-3 motif) and cyclobutane-fused imides, and every molecule of one session's final batch carries a ten- or eleven-membered ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits produce strained three- and four-membered fusions and eight- to twelve-membered rings, and these survive admission into the leading band.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Constrain ring closure by the size and context of the ring being formed: allow five-, six- and seven-membered closures, refuse three- and four-membered rings fused onto an aromatic ring, and cap new macrocyclic closures. The admitted population then grows by ring systems a chemist recognises rather than by strain the scorer cannot see.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session carries 240 C-nitroso groups in 870 proposals while nitro groups appear zero times in all 4350 molecules of all five sessions. N-N single bonds run 10-133 per session, N-O single bonds 28-100, peroxides 7-78. Conventional polar groups are correspondingly rare: carboxylic acids 0-51 per session, and sulfonamides only in the one session whose initial pool supplied an arylsulfonyl fragment (75 of 870, against 0-1 in the other four, with no new one constructed). These bonds sit in the high-scoring band, not only in the tail: nine of twelve digest leaders in one session carry an N-amino amide, and the leaders of another carry three nitroso groups each.
transferable_gaps.gap: Polar functionality is reached through oxidized nitrogen-nitrogen, nitrogen-oxygen and oxygen-oxygen bonds instead of real polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Stock the operator set with conventional polar groups (nitro, sulfonamide, sulfone, carboxylic acid, primary amide, urea) as single edits, and refuse newly created N-N, N-O and O-O single bonds and C-nitroso groups unless an accepted scored parent already carried that environment. A reward for polarity or for heteroatom count is then answered with chemistry rather than with oxidant-like bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five sessions and charged_rate 0.0 on four with 0.0011 on the fifth, while RDKit perceives unassigned stereocentres in 96 percent of one session's molecules, 75, 56 and 36 percent in three more and 9 percent in the last, including the quaternary benzylic carbon of every top-scoring molecule in the session that saturates its objective. No molecule in 4350 is drawn as a salt, zwitterion or quaternary ammonium.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal annotates stereochemistry or formal charge, although most carry stereogenic centres and protonatable nitrogens.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Let the generator set and mutate configuration at the centres it creates, and admit at least one charged form where a basic or acidic centre exists, so configuration and protonation state become searchable degrees of freedom instead of being silently left to whatever the scorer assumes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: With identical operators across the five sessions, the fraction of proposals carrying a basic amine ranges from 0.045 and 0.061 in the two sessions whose survivors lack one to 0.576 and 0.821 in the two whose survivors have one, where every one of the thirty best molecules carries one. In one of the amine-rich sessions the child set contains no piperazine and no piperidine ring at all against 3 and 22 in the paired Parent set, so even saturated amine rings that exist in the lineage can be lost rather than rebuilt.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic amine centres are propagated when the surviving population already has them and are installed de novo at a very low rate.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add explicit operators that install a basic amine centre on an existing ring system (ring nitrogen insertion, saturated amine ring annulation, amine ring-size change) so this feature is reachable from a population that lacks it, instead of depending on the initial molecules to supply it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every session spends evaluations on micro-fragments: 13-32 proposals per session below six heavy atoms, including single atoms and diatomics such as Br, Cl, S, F, FF, ClCl, FBr, C, C=C, C#C, N=O, OO and CC(F)Cl. They land at the bottom of the scale on four objectives (0.0) and at the uninformative floor on the fifth (0.5 for C, Cl, C=C, N=O and N#CCl alike), and they occur as late as evaluation 299.
transferable_gaps.gap: A measurable share of every proposal batch is one- to five-heavy-atom fragments that carry no information back.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enforce a heavy-atom floor, or a minimum fraction of the parent retained, on products of deleting and fragmenting edits, so that the destructive end of the operator distribution cannot reach near-atomic molecules. That returns a few percent of the evaluation budget to molecules that can be compared with the incumbent.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
